classification.difficultyReason: Use marked parallel sides and supplementary co-interior angles to find one or two unknowns.

content.prompt: Using your knowledge of co-interior angles, determine the value of these pronumerals.

spec.description: Tilted parallelogram with 76° at the bottom vertex, a° at the right vertex and b° at the top vertex. One opposite-side pair has single parallel arrows; the other pair has double parallel arrows.
spec.mathematics: Both opposite-side pairs are parallel. The angles a and 76 are co-interior; b and a are co-interior.
spec.answerVisibility: Show only source givens and unknown labels; omit supplied teacher answers.

answer.worked:
Co-interior angles on parallel lines sum to $180^{\circ}$.
$$\begin{align*}a+76&=180\\a&=104\\b+104&=180\\b&=76\end{align*}$$
Therefore $a=104^{\circ}$ and $b=76^{\circ}$.

spec.description: Parallelogram with vertical left and right sides, sloping top and bottom sides, 108° at the upper-left vertex, a° at the lower-left vertex and b° at the upper-right vertex. Vertical sides have single parallel arrows; sloping sides have double parallel arrows.
spec.mathematics: Both opposite-side pairs are parallel. Each unknown forms a co-interior pair with 108°.
spec.answerVisibility: Show only source givens and unknown labels; omit supplied teacher answers.

answer.worked:
Co-interior angles on parallel lines sum to $180^{\circ}$.
$$\begin{align*}a+108&=180\\a&=72\\b+108&=180\\b&=72\end{align*}$$
Therefore $a=72^{\circ}$ and $b=72^{\circ}$.

spec.description: Quadrilateral with only its upper and lower sloping sides marked parallel by matching single arrows. The right-side transversal joins a° at the upper-right vertex and 52° at the lower-right vertex.
spec.mathematics: The two marked sides are parallel; a and 52 are co-interior angles along the right side. No second parallel-side pair is given.
spec.answerVisibility: Show only source givens and unknown labels; omit supplied teacher answer.

answer.worked:
Co-interior angles on parallel lines sum to $180^{\circ}$.
$$\begin{align*}a+52&=180\\a&=128\end{align*}$$
Therefore $a=128^{\circ}$.
